shifts.summary: Overall the shift was reported as Moderate by most sources. Reasoning was generally easy, with many candidates attempting all questions. GA difficulty varied but leaned moderate, while Quant was easy to moderate and English easy. Good attempts ranged from the low 70s to the high 80s.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was described as simple and top‑notch. Options in non‑verbal questions looked similar and were time‑consuming. Statement‑based and blood‑relation items were present.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS questions were tough for some, but many were as expected from previous years. Topics covered history, art, economics, current affairs and specific static GK items.

intro: The analysis for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 9 October 2026 compiles information from three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have been fully reported, showing overall difficulty levels of Moderate and Easy respectively, with good attempt rates ranging from the low 70s to the mid‑80s. Shift 3 is only partially reported; its detailed analysis will be added after the shift is fully evaluated. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as Moderate and Easy respectively, while Shift 3 was described as Moderate to Difficult. The overall difficulty varied across shifts.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were recorded for each shift on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 had good attempts between 72 and 89, Shift 2 reported about 85 good attempts, and Shift 3 showed 85‑90 good attempts. These numbers are unofficial and reflect candidate performance as reported.

faqs.q: Why are the figures for the 9 October 2026 exam considered unofficial?
faqs.a: The figures are based on shift‑wise reports from candidates and third‑party sources, not on the official SSC release. SSC later normalises scores across shifts, which may adjust the final statistics.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for Shift 3 of the 9 October 2026 exam be completed?
faqs.a: Shift 3 is currently marked as partially reported. A complete analysis will be added once the shift’s full data becomes available.

faqs.q: Did time shortage affect any sections in the 9 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: Yes, the reports for Shift 2 indicated that time shortage impacted the Mathematics (Quantitative) section and long passages in English, leading to fewer attempts in those areas.
